question: Under which type of unemployment a person contributes less than their capability?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Disguised unemployment.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disguised unemployment** is a situation where a person appears to be** employed and working,** but their **contribution **to the economy is** less than their capability.**
 
• This type of unemployment often occurs in **agricultural or informal sectors** where there are **too many workers** for the available work, leading to **underemployment.**
 
• Hence, the **correct answer **is option 2, disguised unemployment, where a person contributes less than their capability.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional unemployment **refers to the** temporary **unemployment that occurs when a person is in** between jobs or searching for a job.**
 
• **Compulsory unemployment** is a situation where the government or an employer **forces a person to be unemployed**, such as during a **strike **or due to **discrimination.**
 
• **Cyclical unemployment** is a type of unemployment that occurs due to **fluctuations in the business cycle**, where economic downturns lead to **job losses.**
